Distinguish force (a push/pull) from work (what a force does when it moves an object).
SAY: 
Force is a push or a pull — when you kick a ball, the force moves it forward.
Work is different: work is what happens when a force actually moves something. A machine does work when it moves another object.
So: force can exist without movement (you can push a wall and do no work). Work needs movement.

EXPECTED ANSWER: 
No — there's force, but no movement, so no work.
